subject: SCI
label: Grade 01
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 01 Science, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 7 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.

modules.title: Plants around us
modules.outcome: name parts of a plant and say what plants need
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Plants around us', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: name parts of a plant and say what plants need. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.

Use it: name parts of a plant and say what plants need. Use a diagram, table or short calculation where it fits.
Test and conclude: say what evidence supports your answer and what you would change.
modules.example: Model run for 'Plants around us'. Question: what do we want to find out? Prediction: one sentence. Method: three safe steps with the equipment named. Record: a small table with units. Conclusion: one sentence that uses the evidence and the key words of the unit. What a good answer looks like: a fair test, measured values with units, and a conclusion that matches the table.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Name parts of a plant and say what plants need: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Look at a bean plant growing in a clear cup. Point to and name four parts: root under the soil, stem holding it up, green leaves on the stem, and a flower or bud at the top. Draw it and label each part.

Step 2, Say what each part does. The root drinks water from the soil, the stem carries water up to the leaves, and the leaves use sunlight to make food for the plant. Match each part to its job with a line.

Step 3, Test what plants need. Put two bean seedlings of the same size on a window sill. Water seedling A every day and give it light. Give seedling B no water for five days. Write what you see each day.

Step 4, After five days seedling A is still green and about 8 cm tall. Seedling B is dry, drooping and yellow. Conclusion: a plant needs water to stay healthy. Plants also need light, air and soil to grow well.

Step 5, Try a second case with light. Put one small potted plant in a sunny spot and one inside a dark cupboard for one week, watering both the same. The cupboard plant turns pale and weak, so light matters too.
Step 6, Your turn: name the four parts of a sunflower and say what a sunflower needs to grow. Answer: root, stem, leaf, flower; it needs water, sunlight, air and soil.

modules.title: Animals
modules.outcome: sort animals by where they live and what they eat
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Animals', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: sort animals by where they live and what they eat. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.

modules.example: Solved: A bird lives in a nest, a bee in a hive, a fish in water. Sort animals by where they live: land, water, air. Method: Model run for 'Animals'. Question: what do we want to find out? Prediction: one sentence. Method: three safe steps with the equipment named. Record: a small table with units. Conclusion: one sentence that uses the evidence and the key words of the unit. What a good answer looks like: a fair test, measured values with units, and a conclusion that matches the table.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Sort animals by where they live and what they eat: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Look at six animals: fish, cow, owl, frog, camel and lion. Make three groups by where they live: water, land and air. Fish and frog go in water, cow, camel and lion on land, owl in the air and trees.

Step 2, Sort by what they eat. Cow, camel and rabbit eat only plants, so they are herbivores. Lion and eagle eat other animals, so they are carnivores. Humans and bears eat both, so they are omnivores.

Step 3, Make a table with two columns: Animal and Food. Write cow, grass; lion, meat; hen, grains and insects. Count how many are herbivores. In our list of cow, camel, rabbit, lion and hen there are 3 herbivores, 1 carnivore and 1 omnivore.

Step 4, Explain with a body clue. A cow has flat teeth for grinding grass. A lion has sharp pointed teeth for tearing meat. A fish has fins and gills to live in water. Body parts fit where an animal lives and eats.
Step 5, Conclusion: animals can be grouped by home and by food, and their bodies help them live there. A camel lives in the desert and eats plants, so it goes in land and herbivore.

Step 6, Your turn: sort a duck, a tiger and a goat by home and food. Answer: duck lives in water and on land and is an omnivore; tiger lives on land and is a carnivore; goat lives on land and is a herbivore.
